name: National Executive Council of Papua New Guinea
description: The National Executive Council (NEC), also known as the Cabinet of Papua New Guinea, functions as the policy and decision-making body of the executive branch within the government system of Papua New Guinea. The Prime Minister and Ministers serve as members of the Cabinet.

name: National Parliament of Papua New Guinea
description: The unicameral national legislature of Papua New Guinea. It was created in 1964 as the House of Assembly and gained its current name at independence in 1975. It has 118 seats with 96 open electorates and 22 provincial electorates.

name: Supreme Court of Papua New Guinea
description: The highest court in Papua New Guinea. It is an appellate Full Court of the National Court. The Supreme Court protects constitutional rights and interprets the laws of PNG.

name: Department of Prime Minister and National Executive Council
description: Provides strategic leadership in supporting the government of PNG in development, coordination and implementation of sound policies and programs, and effective governance.

name: Department of Treasury
description: Government department responsible for economic and financial policy advice, managing the national budget, and overseeing fiscal policy in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Finance
description: Government department responsible for financial management, public expenditure, and government accounting in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Foreign Affairs
description: Government department responsible for Papua New Guinea's foreign relations, diplomacy, and international cooperation.

name: Department of Defence
description: Government department responsible for the political oversight of the Papua New Guinea Defence Force and national defence policy.

name: Department of Education
description: Government department responsible for education policy, curriculum development, and management of the national education system in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Health
description: Government department responsible for health policy, public health services, and healthcare delivery in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Works and Highway
description: Government department responsible for infrastructure development, road construction, and highway maintenance in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Justice and Attorney-General
description: Government department responsible for legal affairs, justice administration, and provision of legal advice to the government of Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Petroleum and Energy
description: Government department responsible for the regulation and development of the petroleum and energy sectors in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Mining
description: Government department responsible for regulation and policy in the mining sector of Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Agriculture
description: Government department responsible for agricultural policy, food security, and rural development in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Provincial and Local Level Government Affairs
description: Government department responsible for coordinating and supporting provincial and local-level government administration in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Information and Communication Technology
description: Government department responsible for information and communication technology policy and development in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Forestry
description: Government department responsible for forestry policy, management, and regulation of the forestry sector in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of Fisheries and Marine Resources
description: Government department responsible for fisheries policy, marine resource management, and regulation of the fishing industry in Papua New Guinea.

key_people.title: Minister for Fisheries and Marine Resource
key_people.name: Jelta Wong

name: Department of Transport and Civil Aviation
description: Government department responsible for transport infrastructure and civil aviation regulation in Papua New Guinea.

key_people.title: Minister for Transport and Civil Aviation
key_people.name: Walter Schnaubelt

name: Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology
description: Government department responsible for higher education policy, research, science and technology development in Papua New Guinea.

name: Department of International Trade and Investment
description: Government department responsible for international trade policy, investment promotion, and trade agreements in Papua New Guinea.

key_people.title: Minister for International Trade and Investment
key_people.name: Richard Maru

name: Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary
description: The national police force responsible for maintaining law and order in Papua New Guinea. It has been challenged by advanced weaponry in tribal conflicts and underfunding.

name: Ombudsman Commission of Papua New Guinea
description: Independent constitutional body responsible for investigating complaints about government agencies and officials, and ensuring leadership integrity in Papua New Guinea.

name: Electoral Commission of Papua New Guinea
description: Independent body responsible for conducting national and local elections in Papua New Guinea.

name: Civil Aviation Safety Authority of Papua New Guinea
description: Regulatory body responsible for civil aviation safety oversight in Papua New Guinea.

name: Papua New Guinea Forest Authority
description: Statutory body responsible for the management, regulation, and development of the forestry sector in Papua New Guinea.

name: Kumul Consolidated Holdings
description: The trustee of the General Business Trust that holds, in trust on behalf of the Government and people of Papua New Guinea, the shares of State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) in the non-mining and non-petroleum sectors. Established under the Kumul Consolidated Holdings Act 2002.

name: Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited
description: Papua New Guinea's national petroleum and energy company. Its activities are governed by the Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited Authorisation Act 2015. Holds the state's interests in petroleum projects including the PNG LNG project.

name: Kumul Minerals Holdings Limited
description: State-owned entity holding the government's equity interests in mining projects across Papua New Guinea.

name: PNG Power Limited
description: State-owned electricity utility responsible for generation, transmission, distribution and retailing of electricity throughout Papua New Guinea. Operates three separate grids: Port Moresby system, Ramu grid, and Gazelle Peninsula Grid.

name: Water PNG Limited
description: State-owned water utility responsible for providing water, sewerage, and sanitation services across Papua New Guinea.

name: Air Niugini Limited
description: Papua New Guinea's national airline, operating out of Jacksons International Airport in Port Moresby. Provides domestic and international air services.

name: Telikom PNG Limited
description: Papua New Guinea's 100% state-owned telecommunications company. Formerly a monopoly operator in ICT services until Digicel entered the mobile market in 2007.

name: Post PNG Limited
description: State-owned postal services company providing mail and logistics services throughout Papua New Guinea.

name: PNG Ports Corporation Limited
description: State-owned corporation managing port facilities in Papua New Guinea. Operates 16 of the 22 official ports in the country.

name: National Development Bank
description: State-owned development bank providing financing for economic development, small businesses, and rural enterprises in Papua New Guinea.

name: Motor Vehicles Insurance Limited
description: State-owned insurance company providing compulsory motor vehicle insurance in Papua New Guinea.

name: National Airports Corporation
description: State-owned corporation responsible for operating and managing the 21 national airports in Papua New Guinea, including Jacksons International Airport.

name: Mineral Resources Development Company
description: 100% government-owned company established in 1975 that manages resource equity interests on behalf of landowners and provincial governments in Papua New Guinea.

name: Ok Tedi Mining Limited
description: Major copper and gold producer in Papua New Guinea. The mine is state-run and is a significant economic contributor to Western Province and a major employer.

name: Oil Search Limited
description: Largest oil and gas producer in Papua New Guinea, accounting for over 80% of the country's production. Now merged with Santos Limited. Key partner in the PNG LNG project.

name: ExxonMobil PNG Limited
description: Operator of the PNG LNG joint venture, the largest private-sector investment in the history of PNG. The project includes gas production and processing facilities with capacity of 6.9 million tonnes per year of LNG.

name: Newcrest Mining Limited - Lihir Operations
description: Owner and operator of the Lihir Gold Mine, one of the world's largest and lowest-cost gold mines, located on Lihir Island in Papua New Guinea.

name: Barrick Niugini Limited
description: Owner and operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, one of the largest and longest-running gold mines in Papua New Guinea.

name: New Britain Palm Oil Limited
description: One of the largest companies in Papua New Guinea by revenue ($9.5B), engaged in palm oil production and processing. A major agricultural exporter.

name: Trukai Industries Limited
description: Major manufacturer and distributor of food and beverage products in Papua New Guinea. Produces rice, flour, pasta, and snacks under the popular Trukai brand.

name: Steamships Trading Company Limited
description: One of Papua New Guinea's longest-established companies, operating in shipping, transport, logistics, property, hospitality, and manufacturing.

name: TotalEnergies EP PNG
description: French oil and gas major operating in Papua New Guinea, developing the Papua LNG project based on the Elk-Antelope gas fields.

name: Bank of Papua New Guinea
description: The central bank of Papua New Guinea. Its main function is to issue currency and to act as the banker and financial agent to the Government. It regulates banking and other financial services and manages gold, foreign exchange and international reserves.

name: BSP Financial Group Limited
description: The largest bank in Papua New Guinea and the leading financial institution across the South Pacific. Operates 121 branches in PNG and 7 countries, servicing over 650,000 business banking customers throughout the Pacific.

name: Kina Bank
description: One of the major commercial banks in Papua New Guinea. Formerly Kina Securities, it provides banking, wealth management, and financial services.

name: Westpac Papua New Guinea
description: Subsidiary of Australian Westpac Banking Corporation, providing commercial banking services in Papua New Guinea.

name: ANZ Papua New Guinea
description: Subsidiary of Australia and New Zealand Banking Group, providing commercial and corporate banking services in Papua New Guinea.

name: University of Papua New Guinea
description: The country's first and oldest university, founded in 1965. Located in Port Moresby, it offers programs in medicine, law, business, and the social sciences.

name: Papua New Guinea University of Technology
description: The country's premier technological university located in Lae, Morobe Province. Established in 1965 as PNG Institute of Higher Technical Education. Offers programs in engineering, science, and natural resources management.

name: Divine Word University
description: A national Catholic university in Papua New Guinea. Established by an Act of Parliament in 1980 as Divine Word Institute, and established as a university in 1996. Located in Madang with a campus in Port Moresby.

name: Pacific Adventist University
description: A private Christian university located outside Port Moresby, affiliated with the Seventh-day Adventist Church. Offers programs in various disciplines.

name: University of Goroka
description: A university located in Goroka, Eastern Highlands Province, primarily focused on teacher education and training.

name: Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment
description: A university focused on natural resources and environmental sciences in Papua New Guinea.

name: Institute of National Affairs
description: An independent policy think tank in Papua New Guinea that provides reports on the business and investment environment every five years, highlighting law and order, corruption, and infrastructure issues.

name: Papua New Guinea National Research Institute
description: Papua New Guinea's principal research organization providing policy-relevant research and analysis on national development issues.

name: Post-Courier
description: Papua New Guinea's leading daily newspaper since 1969. With a circulation of 41,000, it is the largest selling Pacific Island newspaper. Majority owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp.

name: The National
description: English language daily newspaper in Papua New Guinea. Owned by Rimbunan Hijau, a Malaysian logging company.

name: National Broadcasting Corporation of Papua New Guinea
description: Papua New Guinea's state-owned national broadcaster. Has been the national broadcaster for over 50 years, operating 22 provincial radio stations nationwide, plus television and online services. Established in 1973.

name: EM TV
description: Papua New Guinea's premier commercial television station, owned by Telikom PNG through its subsidiary Media Niugini Limited. Began operations in 1987 and was the country's only free-to-air TV service until 2008.

name: PNG Media Council
description: Industry body representing media organizations in Papua New Guinea, organizing the annual PNG Media Awards.

name: Transparency International Papua New Guinea
description: PNG chapter of Transparency International, dedicated to fighting corruption, promoting transparency, accountability, and good governance in Papua New Guinea.

name: World Vision Papua New Guinea
description: Global humanitarian organization with over 40 years of experience working in PNG, focusing on helping the most vulnerable children and adults.

name: Centre for Environmental Law and Community Rights
description: Non-governmental organization in Papua New Guinea focused on environmental law, community rights, and educating communities on appropriate ways to manage natural resources. Based in Port Moresby.

name: PNG Tribal Foundation
description: Non-profit organization dedicated to the health and wellness of the people of Papua New Guinea. Partners with provincial leaders, corporations, and fellow NGOs to deliver medical supplies and healthcare support.

name: Papua New Guinea Red Cross Society
description: National Red Cross society of Papua New Guinea, providing disaster relief, health services, and humanitarian assistance.

name: Community Development Forum
description: Civil society organization in Papua New Guinea working on community development and social welfare.

name: Pangu Pati
description: The largest political party in Papua New Guinea with 58 of 118 parliamentary seats. Led by Prime Minister James Marape. Ideology includes indigenism, developmentalism, and economic nationalism.

name: People's National Congress
description: Major political party in Papua New Guinea with 14 of 118 seats. Ideology: populism.

name: United Resources Party
description: Political party in Papua New Guinea with 12 of 118 seats.

name: National Alliance Party
description: Political party in Papua New Guinea with 4 of 118 seats.

name: Social Democratic Party
description: Political party in Papua New Guinea with 4 of 118 seats. Ideology: social democracy.

name: People's First Party
description: Political party in Papua New Guinea with 4 of 118 seats.

name: Papua New Guinea Party
description: Political party in Papua New Guinea with 3 of 118 seats. Founded in 2007 by former Prime Minister Mekere Morauta.

name: Papua New Guinea Defence Force
description: The military organisation responsible for the defence of Papua New Guinea. Originated from the Australian Army land forces of the territory of Papua New Guinea, coming into being in January 1973. Consists of Land Element, Air Element, and Maritime Element with around 4,000 active personnel.

name: Asian Development Bank - Papua New Guinea Office
description: International development bank providing financial assistance and development programs in Papua New Guinea, including the State-Owned Enterprises Reform Program.

name: World Bank Papua New Guinea
description: International financial institution providing development assistance and lending to Papua New Guinea. Approved a US$100 million operation in June 2021 to support PNG's COVID-19 response.

name: United Nations Papua New Guinea
description: United Nations country team in Papua New Guinea, coordinating various UN agencies' development, humanitarian, and peace-building programs.
